verdict.rationale: First-party docs show that Hightouch runs on top of the customer's warehouse without copying data into a separate system. Data teams define models in SQL, from tables or views, or by reusing dbt models. Audiences are built from warehouse data, and modeled data syncs to 300+ destinations with CDC. A community report independently corroborates that no data is stored in Hightouch and that SQL models drive declarative syncs. Missing for 10: hands-on independent testing that confirms the end-to-end warehouse-native activation flow in practice.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can run warehouse-native: define models and audiences on tables already in my warehouse and activate them without re-collecting the data (reverse ETL)

citations.quote: It runs on top of your data warehouse, so teams can use customer data without copying it into a separate system.
Data teams typically create models by writing SQL in the editor, selecting from tables or views, or re-using dbt models and BI queries from Looker or Sigma.
Create audiences from warehouse data, build automated journeys
Sync modeled data to sales, support, analytics, and internal tools on a schedule or when data changes.
Hightouch's hybrid architecture stores no data in Hightouch itself out of the box—it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket
